summary.text: Republican Robert Short won the election for Secretary of State of Wyoming on November 3, 2026, defeating Bryan McCarty, and is set to take office when the new term begins.
A Converse County commissioner since 2014 and a Douglas businessman, he won the August 18 Republican primary over several candidates including Freedom Caucus chair Rachel Williams.

paragraphs.text: Robert Short grew up in Glenrock, Wyoming.
He took his first job at age 12 on a ranch, went to work in the oil patch at 16, in power-line construction at 17 and in a uranium mine at 18, and stayed there until it closed.
Short then studied electrical engineering and computer science, worked in technology, and was recruited into a 20-year career in nuclear science.

In 2004 he started businesses in Douglas and Glenrock; his campaign site says he returned to Douglas with his family in 2005 and that the businesses have since grown to span energy, agriculture, retail and tourism and more than 120 jobs.
Short was first elected to the Converse County Commission in 2014 and has since been re-elected twice.
He is vice president of the Wyoming County Commissioners Association and has served on several state boards and as an election judge.
He won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary after raising far more than his opponents, according to WyoFile, and about half of the roughly $430,000 he had raised before it came from loans.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 67.8% of the vote to Bryan McCarty's 23.8%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
